cards.subject: An empty lake
lines: Omen and the Lunar Festival did not ship with the game. They arrive in January 2006.
Before that there was nothing under the water at all. Anyone who played the launch year knew a quieter valley than this one.

cards.subject: Druids get in for nothing
lines: They learn it at level ten, and they get it the moment they accept the quest — before ever setting foot in the place.
Every other class in the game walks.
There is no return teleport. You leave by flight master or on foot.

cards.subject: The flights only go one way
lines: Nighthaven's two flight masters are druid-only. Ask as anything else and you get told: "You're not a druid!"
Neither is a destination — Moonglade cannot be selected from any other flight master anywhere in the world.
Both factions' masters stand together, serving nobody but druids.

cards.subject: The only door is a fight
lines: The single walking route in is the furbolg tunnel, which also links Felwood and Winterspring.
The Timbermaw attack strangers until you have ground their reputation up.
The overland entrance to the most peaceful zone in the game is a corridor of angry bears.

cards.subject: There is nothing to kill
lines: Outside of event content there are no hostile mobs here. No useful herb, no ore node, nothing skinnable.
It is the only sizeable outdoor zone in the game that gives a player with a weapon nothing whatsoever to do.

cards.subject: The peace is a convention
lines: Sanctuary zones do not exist yet — that flag arrives with Burning Crusade. Moonglade is contested territory.
Nothing mechanically stops a level sixty from killing the level ten druid who just teleported in.
Everyone behaves anyway, which is the interesting part.

cards.subject: The Great Bear Spirit
lines: The level ten Bear Form quest sends every druid in the game to this one spot.
Click it and the text reads: "The bear looks at you calmly and patiently, but says nothing."

cards.subject: Keeper Remulos
cards.tag: Stag body, antlers, one wooden hand
lines: A son of Cenarius, and brother to the one buried under Maraudon.
He ran the Cenarion Circle with Fandral Staghelm and Hamuul Runetotem while Malfurion slept.
He is the reason there are tauren druids. He let them in when Staghelm would not.

cards.subject: Nighthaven
lines: Night elf stonework on the shore of the lake, two moonwells, and a settlement built out over the water itself.
It is sequestered by design — a town for people who can teleport.
Once a year, for the Lunar Festival, it opens to everybody.

cards.subject: Lake Elune'ara
lines: The purest water on Kalimdor, said to reflect starlight, and possibly blessed by Elune herself.
Warcraft III's version of this lake had islands in it.
This one has none. The water is unbroken.

cards.subject: The man asleep under your feet
lines: Malfurion's body lies in his barrow den here for the whole of this game — comatose, his spirit lost in the Emerald Dream.
There is no Malfurion in Moonglade. You can walk into the dens and there is nothing to find.
He does not stand up in the world for another five years.

cards.subject: The night he came out of the sky
lines: Remulos opens a portal into the Dream over the lake and Eranikus comes through it.
Forty players hold the shrine against Nightmare Phantasms — and must not kill him. Tyrande arrives with her priestesses and redeems him instead.
One of the very few scripted world events this game ever staged outdoors.

cards.subject: Why a zone with no mobs has traffic
lines: Almost everybody in Moonglade at any given moment is a druid passing through.
Teleport in, take the druid-only flight out to Thunder Bluff or Rut'theran.
It is a free second hearthstone on a thirty-minute cooldown, and it is the whole economy of the place.
